soru: Bilişim eğitiminde üretken yapay zeka kullanımının zararları ve istenmeyen sonuçları (akademik dürüstlük, öğrenme kaybı, bağımlılık) üzerine en önemli çalışmalar ve açık problemler neler?
istem:
Research question: Bilişim eğitiminde üretken yapay zeka kullanımının zararları ve istenmeyen sonuçları (akademik dürüstlük, öğrenme kaybı, bağımlılık) üzerine en önemli çalışmalar ve açık problemler neler?

Cutoff date: 2025-09-06. Only works published BEFORE this date count.

List the 30 most important works (papers) for this research question that were published before the cutoff date, in order of importance (most important first) — the kind a careful expert survey published right after the cutoff would cite. Give each with its arXiv id and/or DOI.

You MUST research this with web search rather than answer from memory: search for the important works, and verify each listed work's title, publication date and identifier on the web (e.g. arxiv.org, doi.org, the publisher or DBLP page) before including it.

When you are done, reply with ONLY a JSON object in this form (no other text):
{"calismalar": [{"sira": 1, "baslik": "exact title", "yil": 2020, "arxiv_id": "arXiv id or null", "doi": "DOI or null", "gerekce": "one sentence on why this work is important"}]}
with exactly 30 items. If you do not know an identifier, use null instead of guessing.

calismalar.baslik: The Widening Gap: The Benefits and Harms of Generative AI for Novice Programmers
calismalar.gerekce: ICER 2024 study using observation, interviews and eye tracking; it shows that GenAI helps students who already understand the material, while weaker novices build metacognitive difficulties and a false sense of progress.

calismalar.baslik: The Robots are Here: Navigating the Generative AI Revolution in Computing Education
calismalar.gerekce: ITiCSE working group report combining a literature review, surveys, educator interviews and an ethics framing; it set out the main risks of LLMs in computing education, including integrity, over-reliance and assessment.

calismalar.baslik: Programming Is Hard - Or at Least It Used to Be: Educational Opportunities and Challenges of AI Code Generation
calismalar.gerekce: SIGCSE 2023 position paper that set the agenda on the challenges AI code generation poses for academic integrity, assessment and learning.

calismalar.baslik: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
calismalar.gerekce: Large field experiment (PNAS) giving causal evidence of learning loss: unrestricted GPT access raised practice performance, but grades fell by 17% once access was removed.

calismalar.baslik: Studying the effect of AI Code Generators on Supporting Novice Learners in Introductory Programming
calismalar.gerekce: CHI 2023 controlled experiment measuring how Codex affects novices' performance and retention; it is foundational to the over-reliance debate.

calismalar.baslik: AI Meets the Classroom: When Do Large Language Models Harm Learning?
calismalar.gerekce: Observational and experimental evidence from programming courses that using LLMs to get solutions harms learning, using them as tutors helps, and students overestimate their gains.

calismalar.baslik: From "Ban It Till We Understand It" to "Resistance is Futile": How University Programming Instructors Plan to Adapt as More Students Use AI Code Generation and Explanation Tools such as ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot
calismalar.gerekce: ICER 2023 interview study documenting instructors' concerns about cheating and learning loss and the strategies they planned in response.

calismalar.baslik: Computing Education in the Era of Generative AI
calismalar.gerekce: CACM article summarizing the challenges code-generation models pose for introductory programming teaching, including integrity, over-reliance and bias.

calismalar.baslik: The Robots Are Coming: Exploring the Implications of OpenAI Codex on Introductory Programming
calismalar.gerekce: First widely cited demonstration that Codex can solve CS1 exam questions, raising the first alarm about academic integrity and assessment.

calismalar.baslik: How Novices Use LLM-Based Code Generators to Solve CS1 Coding Tasks in a Self-Paced Learning Environment
calismalar.gerekce: Shows that generating a whole solution from a single prompt gives the highest authoring success but the weakest code-modification performance, documenting the cost of over-reliance.

calismalar.baslik: Beware of metacognitive laziness: Effects of generative artificial intelligence on learning motivation, processes, and performance
calismalar.gerekce: Randomized study introducing the concept of 'metacognitive laziness': GenAI improves task performance without improving knowledge gain or motivation.

calismalar.baslik: Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task
calismalar.gerekce: EEG preprint that put the 'cognitive debt' idea into wide discussion; it reports weaker neural connectivity and weaker ownership of their own work among LLM users.

calismalar.baslik: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported Reductions in Cognitive Effort and Confidence Effects From a Survey of Knowledge Workers
calismalar.gerekce: CHI 2025 survey finding that confidence in GenAI is associated with less critical thinking; it is a key reference for work on dependence and deskilling.

calismalar.baslik: Beyond the Hype: A Comprehensive Review of Current Trends in Generative AI Research, Teaching Practices, and Tools
calismalar.gerekce: ITiCSE 2024 working group systematic review and survey; the most comprehensive summary of GenAI research, teaching practice and open problems in computing education.

calismalar.baslik: Generative AI in Computing Education: Perspectives of Students and Instructors
calismalar.gerekce: Compares student and instructor views on over-reliance, plagiarism and assessment, revealing tensions between the two groups.

calismalar.baslik: Self-Regulation, Self-Efficacy, and Fear of Failure Interactions with How Novices Use LLMs to Solve Programming Problems
calismalar.gerekce: Shows that students with low self-efficacy and high fear of failure turn to AI more and earlier, explaining who is at risk of dependence.

calismalar.baslik: Detecting ChatGPT-Generated Code Submissions in a CS1 Course Using Machine Learning Models
calismalar.gerekce: A core study on technical detection of AI-generated code for academic integrity.

calismalar.baslik: Detecting LLM-Generated Text in Computing Education: A Comparative Study for ChatGPT Cases
calismalar.gerekce: Compares eight AI-text detectors on computing education data and shows their unreliability and high false-positive rates, which bears on integrity policy.

calismalar.baslik: Thrilled by Your Progress! Large Language Models (GPT-4) No Longer Struggle to Pass Assessments in Higher Education Programming Courses
calismalar.gerekce: Shows that GPT-4 passes the assessments of entire programming courses, undermining the validity of traditional assessment.

calismalar.baslik: "It's Weird That it Knows What I Want": Usability and Interactions with Copilot for Novice Programmers
calismalar.gerekce: First observational study of novices using Copilot; it documents cognitive and metacognitive difficulties and interaction patterns.

calismalar.baslik: How Do Programming Students Use Generative AI?
calismalar.gerekce: FSE 2025 experiment showing that most students who use the chatbot ask for complete solutions and get stuck in a cycle of submitting wrong code and asking for fixes, a loss of agency.

calismalar.baslik: Does ChatGPT Help With Introductory Programming? An Experiment of Students Using ChatGPT in CS1
calismalar.gerekce: Controlled CS1 experiment finding no significant learning gain from ChatGPT and much less use of other resources by its users.

calismalar.baslik: The Effects of Generative AI on Computing Students' Help-Seeking Preferences
calismalar.gerekce: Examines how GenAI changes students' help-seeking from instructors and peers, and the emerging skill gap in using it.

calismalar.baslik: Trust in Generative AI among Students: An Exploratory Study
calismalar.gerekce: Survey of 253 students at two universities on how much they trust GenAI and how their confidence and motivation differ, the basis of calibrated trust and dependence.

calismalar.baslik: Instructor Perceptions of AI Code Generation Tools - A Multi-Institutional Interview Study
calismalar.gerekce: Multi-country interview study of instructors' integrity and learning concerns and their planned adaptations.

calismalar.baslik: CodeHelp: Using Large Language Models with Guardrails for Scalable Support in Programming Classes
calismalar.gerekce: Pioneering design response that uses guardrails to prevent over-reliance by not giving away full solutions.

calismalar.baslik: CodeAid: Evaluating a Classroom Deployment of an LLM-based Programming Assistant that Balances Student and Educator Needs
calismalar.gerekce: Classroom deployment with about 700 students of an assistant that does not reveal code; it evaluates the balance between student and educator needs.

calismalar.baslik: Exploring the Design Space of Cognitive Engagement Techniques with AI-Generated Code for Enhanced Learning
calismalar.gerekce: Experimentally compares cognitive engagement techniques against the 'illusion of learning' that AI-generated code creates.

calismalar.baslik: Is it harmful or helpful? Examining the causes and consequences of generative AI usage among university students
calismalar.gerekce: Multi-wave study linking ChatGPT use to procrastination, memory loss and lower academic performance.

calismalar.baslik: The Impact of Large Language Models on Programming Education and Student Learning Outcomes
calismalar.gerekce: Ten-week study measuring how informal LLM use in software development relates to student performance.
